title: Contact Group 51/49: Mostar's Response
sources: ICTY Prlić et al. Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), 29 May 2013
content:
In July 1994 the Contact Group presented its 51/49 framework to the Bosnian Croat leadership. For Herceg-Bosna the map was less a concession than a ratification: the Washington Agreement of March 1994 had already folded the Croat war aim into the Federation entity, and the 51/49 plan fixed that Federation at 51 percent of Bosnian territory with Croat constitutive-nation status preserved inside it.

The Prlić judgment records the HR HB Presidency responding to the Contact Group through the Federation channel rather than as an independent party — a posture Zagreb directed. The Tuđman presidential transcripts admitted at Prlić show Croatia treating the 51/49 map as the architecture within which the Croat political project would survive: not a parallel Herceg-Bosna state, but constitutive status in a Federation that the great powers now guaranteed.

Historically Mostar accepted, in alignment with Zagreb and the Washington framework. The alternative postures — rejecting the map, or accepting it with amendments protecting Croat territorial autonomy — would have reopened the question the Washington Agreement had only just closed: whether Herceg-Bosna would pursue its claims inside the Federation or against it.

The posture recorded here conditions the durability of the Croat-Bosniak Federation through the 1995 endgame and into Dayton.
